# EduBox roadmap

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-29-edubox-phase1-prototype-design.md
Git authority: phase-branch commits yes; each phase is one branch `phase-N` off `main` (the GitHub default branch; local `master` is obsolete); after a passed gate: push `phase-N`, open a PR to `main`, wait for CI green, merge with a merge commit, tag `phase-N-done`: yes
Stack: Flutter (Android tablet, Vietnamese UI via Flutter l10n/ARB, local store SQLite via drift plus an outbox) + a self-written Dart server on Serverpod 4.0.4 (generated typed client, `serverpod_auth_idp` email/password sign-in, streaming methods, Redis disabled) with PostgreSQL and S3-compatible object storage (MinIO locally); everything runs locally through Docker Compose, no cloud account, no billing; OpenRouter mocked (an optional real key goes only in the git-ignored `edubox_server/config/passwords.yaml`)
Commands: build `(cd edubox_server && serverpod generate && dart build cli --target bin/main.dart --output build) && (cd edubox_flutter && flutter build apk --debug)` | lint `(cd edubox_server && dart analyze --fatal-infos && dart format --output=none --set-exit-if-changed .) && (cd edubox_flutter && flutter analyze && dart format --output=none --set-exit-if-changed .)` | test `tool/bootstrap.sh && docker compose up -d --wait postgres_test minio && docker compose run --rm minio-init && (cd edubox_fixtures && dart test) && (cd edubox_server && dart test --coverage=coverage && dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov --in=coverage --out=coverage/lcov.info --report-on=lib && dart run ../tool/coverage_gate.dart coverage/lcov.info) && (cd edubox_flutter && flutter test)` | e2e `tool/bootstrap.sh && docker compose --profile e2e up -d --build --wait && docker compose run --rm minio-init && (cd edubox_flutter && flutter test integration_test -d $EDUBOX_E2E_DEVICE --dart-define=EDUBOX_SERVER_URL=http://10.0.2.2:8080/)` (the integration test resets state through `e2e.run`)

Prerequisites (installed by the user, not by the pipeline):
- Flutter SDK (stable, which includes Dart) with the Android toolchain, Android SDK, and an x86_64 tablet AVD named `edubox_tablet` (API 34 or newer).
- JDK 21 or newer (Android Gradle builds).
- Docker with Compose v2 (Docker 29 is installed).
- Serverpod CLI 4.0.4, the same version as every `serverpod*` package: `dart pub global activate serverpod_cli 4.0.4` (a per-user Dart tool, not a system install; the pipeline may run it if it is missing).

Notes on commands:
- Bootstrap: `tool/bootstrap.sh` (idempotent) copies the committed `edubox_server/config/passwords.example.yaml` to the git-ignored `edubox_server/config/passwords.yaml` when that file is missing, and never overwrites it. The example holds only clearly labelled dev-only values for the local stack (database, MinIO, Serverpod auth secrets) in the `development` and `test` sections, and no production section. The real OpenRouter key is the only secret a developer may add by hand, and only to their own `passwords.yaml`.
- Code generation: run `serverpod generate` in `edubox_server/` after any model or endpoint change; it regenerates the server protocol, `edubox_client`, and the Serverpod test tools.
- Migrations: run `serverpod create-migration` in `edubox_server/` after any table change and commit the migration; the server applies migrations at start with `--apply-migrations` (the compose `server` service does this).
- Compose services: `postgres` and `minio` (no profile; always started), `postgres_test` (no profile; the throwaway database for Serverpod's test tools), `server` (profile `e2e`; built from `edubox_server/Dockerfile`, mounts `edubox_server/config` read-only, applies migrations, and has a healthcheck that passes only after migrations are applied and the API answers), and the one-shot services `minio-init` and `seed` (profile `tools`, never started by `up`, only through `docker compose run --rm`). Serverpod's default Redis services are removed and Redis is disabled in every run-mode config.
- `minio-init` creates the private buckets for development, test, and e2e (idempotent) with the dev-only MinIO credentials; nothing else creates buckets.
- `seed` runs after the `server` healthcheck passes; it resets data by truncating every EduBox data table and the Serverpod auth tables (never dropping the schema or touching migration bookkeeping) and emptying the e2e bucket, then creates the demo accounts (email/password, server-stored role, parent link), classes with `gradeLevel`, `subjects[]`, and membership, the not-set-up fixtures, and fixture content used by E2E tests; every e2e run starts from this fresh state. The on-device test triggers the same reset and the reconnect/role deltas through the token-guarded `e2e.run` route because it cannot run a host command. E2E uses the development database and bucket, so an e2e run wipes local development data.
- `EDUBOX_E2E_DEVICE` is the device ID of the running `edubox_tablet` AVD as printed by `flutter devices` (normally `emulator-5554`); start it first with `flutter emulators --launch edubox_tablet`.
- The Android emulator reaches the host's compose stack at `10.0.2.2` (server on 8080, MinIO on 9000); the app reads the server URL from a backend config object whose default comes from `EDUBOX_SERVER_URL`, and an integration test file may construct its own config object to override it.
- `dart test` in `edubox_server/` runs unit tests and endpoint integration tests through Serverpod's test tools (`withServerpod`, real PostgreSQL and MinIO, authenticated and unauthenticated callers through `AuthenticationOverride`).
- Coverage gates (80% minimum): `tool/coverage_gate.dart` (created in phase 1) reads `coverage/lcov.info`, excludes generated code (`lib/src/generated/**`), and fails when the grading, rate-limit, lockout, or authorization source directories are under 80% line coverage each; a directory that does not exist yet is skipped, but a directory that exists with no lcov records fails.
- Paths `edubox_server/`, `edubox_client/`, `edubox_flutter/` (Serverpod's default layout), the compose file at the repo root (`compose.yaml`), the scripts under `tool/`, the gated source directories, and the service names above are an ASSUMPTION; the phase 1 contract-architect may rename them and must update these commands.

## Status

| Phase | Goal | Status | Branch | Contract tag | Gate round | Updated |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Each role signs in to a Vietnamese UI and lands on its own home, also offline from the local store; student sees only approved content; a streaming server method and MinIO round trip are proven | building | phase-1 | - | - | 2026-10-29 |
| 2 | Teacher uploads and approves content; student reads, watches, and downloads it for offline use | planned | - | - | - | - |
| 3 | Teacher assigns a lesson-linked practice exercise; student submits (online or offline through the outbox); auto-grade result shows on the teacher dashboard | planned | - | - | - | - |
| 4 | Student chats with a streaming, scoped, rate-limited AI tutor; every exchange is logged by the server | planned | - | - | - | - |
| 5 | Student takes a timed test with online start, auto-submit, offline survival, late flagging, and the AI tutor locked out | planned | - | - | - | - |
| 6 | Parent reads the linked child's results and full AI transcripts; teacher reviews AI chats of own classes | planned | - | - | - | - |

Status values, in order: planned, shaping, contracting, planning, building, integrating, reviewing, fixing, done.
`blocked` can replace any of them when a deadlock stops the phase; only the user's decision clears it.

## Phase 1: Role-gated sign-in, approved library, and backend round trip (walking skeleton)

- Outcome (demoable): On the `edubox_tablet` AVD talking to the local compose stack, a seeded student, teacher, and parent each sign in through a Vietnamese UI and land on their own role home; each home still renders from the local store when offline and refreshes on reconnect; the student's library lists only approved content for the student's classes; integration tests prove a Serverpod streaming method reaches the app and the server can store and read an object in MinIO.
- Screens: `sign-in`, `account-not-set-up` (signed-in auth user with no EduBox profile or no valid role), `student-home`, `student-library`, `teacher-home`, `parent-home` (placeholder showing the linked child's name only); plus the shell's offline and reconnecting strip
- Backend capabilities:
  - Serverpod 4.0.4 project (`edubox_server`, `edubox_client`, `edubox_flutter`), Docker Compose stack (PostgreSQL, PostgreSQL for tests, MinIO, server, `minio-init`, `seed`; Redis disabled), first migrations, `tool/bootstrap.sh`, committed dev-only `passwords.example.yaml`, and `tool/coverage_gate.dart`.
  - Account provisioning by the seed/admin script only: `serverpod_auth_idp` email/password auth users, EduBox `users` rows with `role` (`student|teacher|parent`) and, for parents, `linkedStudentId` and `linkedStudentName`.
  - No self-service accounts: the email identity endpoint exposes sign-in only; account registration, account requests, and password reset are not exposed in the generated client, or, where the module base class forces them, are overridden to always deny.
  - Tables `users`, `classes` (with `gradeLevel` and `subjects[]`), class membership, `content` (metadata fixtures with `status: draft|approved` and class scope), all seeded, plus two not-set-up fixtures: an auth user with no `users` row and a `users` row whose `role` is null.
  - Endpoints: email sign-in (module), `profile.me`, `classes.mine` (teacher's own classes), `content.library` (student: approved content of their classes only).
  - `profile.me` returns a typed result: `ready` with the caller's own profile (role, name, and for parents the linked child's name), or `notSetUp` when the caller has no `users` row, a null role, or a stored role value the server cannot parse; it never answers `notSetUp` with a server error.
  - Server-side authorization layer: every EduBox endpoint method resolves the caller's session and loads the role from `users` before touching data; unauthenticated and wrong-role callers get a named error; the client never decides access.
  - Authorization test matrix: every EduBox endpoint method has an allowed-caller test and a denied-caller test (wrong role, other class, unauthenticated); the auth module's methods are listed separately, each either on the explicit unauthenticated exception list (sign-in, plus the module's session refresh method if the chosen session mode has one) with a test, or with a test proving it denies; a check fails when a generated endpoint method appears in neither list.
  - A minimal streaming method `diagnostics.pingStream` (authenticated; streams three messages carrying the caller's role, then closes) to prove the Serverpod streaming path from the compose stack to the Android app before phase 4 depends on it.
  - Object-storage spike: Serverpod storage (`serverpod_cloud_storage_s3_compat` 4.0.4, see the 2026-10-30 ruling) configured against MinIO with a private bucket and a configurable public endpoint, proven by a server integration test that stores, reads back, and issues a short-lived signed URL for a tiny object.
  - Flutter app shell: backend config object (server URL), session persistence through the auth module's client session manager, role-based routing from `profile.me`, design tokens from `docs/design/app-direction.md`.
  - Local store (drift) for cached metadata: profile and role, the student's library items, the teacher's class list, the parent's linked child name; screens read from the local store and refresh from the server when online and on every offline-to-online transition.
  - Network seam: an app-level `NetworkController` whose offline mode makes every server call fail fast as offline and drives every offline UI state (the shell's `networkOffline` strip and its `networkReconnecting` state); its production source combines connectivity events with a server reachability probe, and tests switch it directly.
  - Localization scaffolding: `flutter_localizations`, `intl`, `l10n.yaml`, template ARB `app_vi.arb`, `vi` as the only supported and default locale, `intl` date and number formatting in `vi`.
- Exit criteria:
  1. E2E: seeded student signs in and sees exactly the approved fixtures for their classes in `student-library`; the seeded draft fixture and another class's approved fixture are absent.
  2. E2E: seeded teacher signs in and lands on `teacher-home` listing their own classes; seeded parent signs in and lands on `parent-home` showing the linked child's name.
  3. E2E: the seeded auth user with no `users` row and the seeded user with a null role each land on `account-not-set-up` showing l10n key `accountNotSetUp` (vi: "Tài khoản chưa được thiết lập") with check-again and sign-out actions, never on a role home; server integration test: a `users` row whose role column holds an unknown value (written with raw SQL) makes `profile.me` return `notSetUp`, not an error.
  4. E2E: wrong credentials show l10n key `signInWrongCredentials` (vi: "Email hoặc mật khẩu không đúng"); a dedicated integration test file constructs its own backend config object pointing at a closed port on `10.0.2.2` (overriding the `EDUBOX_SERVER_URL` default) and asserts l10n key `backendUnreachable` (vi: "Không kết nối được với EduBox") with a `retry` action (vi: "Thử lại").
  5. E2E (offline with cache): for each role in turn, the user signs in online and the role home loads; the network seam is switched offline and the app root is re-created (drift database closed and reopened from disk); the signed-in session is restored from local storage without contacting the server, and `student-home` plus `student-library`, `teacher-home`, and `parent-home` render the cached data with the `networkOffline` strip.
  6. E2E (offline without cache): the user signs in online, the test clears the drift cache tables for that role's home data, switches the seam offline, and re-creates the app root; `student-home` shows `studentHomeLibraryOfflineNoCache`, `student-library` shows `libraryOfflineNoData`, `teacher-home` shows `teacherClassesOfflineNoData`, and `parent-home` shows `parentHomeOfflineNoData`, never an empty state.
  7. E2E (reconnect): with a home rendered offline, the server-side fixture is changed (a new approved item, or a new class for the teacher), the seam is switched online, the strip shows `networkReconnecting` and then collapses, and the home shows the new data without user action.
  8. Unit tests: the seam's production source maps connectivity events and reachability probe results to online and offline, including "network connected but server unreachable" as offline and recovery when the probe succeeds again; probe failures never throw into the UI.
  9. E2E: an integration test running on the AVD calls `diagnostics.pingStream` through the generated client against the compose stack at `10.0.2.2`, receives at least two messages before the stream closes, and the messages carry the signed-in user's role.
  10. Server integration test: the storage spike stores an object in the test bucket created by `minio-init`, reads it back byte-identical, issues a signed URL (for a configurable public endpoint) that fetches the object, and a direct unsigned request to the bucket is denied.
  11. Server authorization tests: a student calling `content.library` never receives draft content or another class's content; `profile.me` returns only the caller's own profile; a student or parent calling `classes.mine` is denied; no endpoint lets a client change `role`, class membership, or the parent link; every EduBox endpoint method rejects unauthenticated callers.
  12. Server integration test (no sign-up): calling every exposed registration, account-request, or password-reset method of the auth module (if any is exposed) is denied, no auth user and no `users` row is created, and the generated client offers no sign-up call that succeeds; sign-in is the only unauthenticated call that succeeds.
  13. Server authorization test: changing a user's `role` in the `users` table changes what that user's next call may do, without signing in again (the role is read server-side, never trusted from the client).
  14. Authorization code coverage is at least 80% as reported by `tool/coverage_gate.dart`, and the authorization matrix check passes.
  15. l10n: every user-visible string in `edubox_flutter/lib/` comes from `AppLocalizations`; a test fails on string literals passed to `Text`, semantics labels, hints, or tooltips outside generated l10n code; E2E assertions look strings up with `lookupAppLocalizations(Locale('vi'))` instead of hardcoding text.
  16. Lint, test, and e2e commands (including `tool/bootstrap.sh`) pass in a clean checkout on a machine with only the listed prerequisites (no cloud account, no billing, no hand-made secrets file).
  17. Flutter accessibility guideline tests (`androidTapTargetGuideline`, `labeledTapTargetGuideline`, `textContrastGuideline`) pass on every phase 1 screen in its loaded, loading, empty, error, and offline states.
- Depends on: none
- Risks:
  - The AVD reaching the host compose stack at `10.0.2.2` (cleartext HTTP and WebSocket allowed only in debug builds) is the first integration that can fail; if `integration_test` cannot drive the stack reliably, the E2E strategy changes.
  - Serverpod streaming methods run over a WebSocket; if they are unreliable from the AVD through `10.0.2.2`, phase 4 needs another streaming transport, which is a contract change; finding that here is the point of criterion 9.
  - `serverpod_cloud_storage_s3_compat` may not support a custom endpoint and path-style addressing for MinIO; the fallback is a small custom storage implementation on a generic S3 client; finding that here is the point of criterion 10.
  - Signed URLs embed the host the server signs for; MinIO's public endpoint must be `10.0.2.2:9000` for the AVD while the server reaches it as `minio:9000` inside compose, and host-side tests use `localhost:9000`.
  - Offline session restore: criterion 5 and the student sign-out warning assume the auth module's client session manager restores a stored session without a server round trip; if it validates or refreshes online first, the app needs its own offline session handling, which is a contract change.
  - The auth module's base email endpoint may force registration and reset methods into the generated client; they must be overridden to deny, or sign-up becomes possible (criterion 12 guards this).
  - The role is loaded per request; any per-session caching added for speed must be invalidated on role change or criterion 13 fails.
  - Display and body fonts (Bitter, Be Vietnam Pro, IBM Plex Mono) must be bundled with full Vietnamese diacritic coverage.

## Phase 2: Teacher publishes content, student studies it offline

- Outcome (demoable): A teacher uploads a PDF e-book and a video, approves them for a class, and the student opens the e-book and plays the video, downloads them, then reads the e-book with the app offline.
- Screens: `teacher-content-list`, `teacher-content-upload`, `teacher-content-detail` (preview plus approve action), `student-content-detail` (with download state), `student-ebook-reader`, `student-video-player`
- Backend capabilities:
  - Upload flow through Serverpod's file upload: `content.createUpload` authorizes the teacher for the target class and returns an upload description for a per-teacher, per-class path in the private MinIO bucket with size and MIME limits; the client uploads directly; `content.completeUpload` verifies the upload.
  - Content ingest (the spec's "contentIngest", now server code run by `content.completeUpload`) with the scope fixed in Rulings: validates type (PDF, EPUB, MP4), size, and readability; normalizes metadata (MIME, size, page count or duration); sets the content's ingest status (`processing|ready|rejected` plus reason); logs failures server-side.
  - `content.approve`: only the owning teacher moves content from `draft` to `approved`; approved content becomes visible to students through `content.library`.
  - `content.fileUrl`: issues a short-lived signed URL only to a student of a class the approved content belongs to, or to its owning teacher; the bucket itself is never readable without a signature.
  - Local content cache: downloaded files in the app's file cache, cache index and content metadata in the drift store from phase 1.
  - Named l10n states for upload progress, ingest failure with retry, and download status.
- Exit criteria:
  1. E2E: teacher uploads a fixture PDF and MP4 from `teacher-content-upload`; both reach `ready` in `teacher-content-list`; the teacher approves both; the student then sees both in `student-library`.
  2. E2E: student opens the e-book and `student-ebook-reader` shows page 1 with a page indicator whose total equals the fixture's page count; student opens the video and `student-video-player` reports a duration greater than zero and a playback position that advances.
  3. E2E: student downloads the e-book; with the network seam switched offline, the e-book still opens from cache and `student-content-detail` shows l10n key `contentAvailableOffline` (vi: "Đã tải về máy"); a not-downloaded item shows `contentNeedsInternet` (vi: "Cần kết nối mạng để mở") instead of a spinner.
  4. Server integration test: completing an upload of a disallowed file type or an oversize file marks the content `rejected` with a reason; widget test: the teacher UI shows that reason with a replace action; authorization test: rejected content is never returned to students.
  5. Server authorization tests (allowed and denied caller per method): student cannot call `content.createUpload`, `content.completeUpload`, or `content.approve`; teacher cannot create an upload for, or approve content of, another teacher's class; `content.fileUrl` is denied for draft or rejected content to students, for another class's student, and for parents; no client-facing method can set ingest status or normalized metadata.
  6. Server integration test: a direct unsigned request to an uploaded object in MinIO is denied, and an expired signed URL is rejected.
  7. E2E: an upload started while the network seam is offline shows l10n key `uploadFailed` (vi: "Tải lên thất bại") with a `retry` action, and retry after switching online completes the upload.
  8. Unit and widget tests cover the cache index (download, evict, lookup) and the offline and online content states; authorization code coverage stays at least 80%; Flutter accessibility guideline tests pass on every phase 2 screen.
- Depends on: Phase 1
- Risks:
  - EPUB rendering in Flutter is less mature than PDF; may force a DECISION to ship PDF-only in phase 2 and EPUB later.
  - Reading page count and duration server-side needs PDF and MP4 parsing in Dart (or a tool like `ffprobe` in the server image); a heavy dependency or slow ingest may move ingest to a Serverpod future call.
  - Video seeking through signed URLs needs MinIO range requests; large videos strain tablet storage; cache size limits and eviction may need a contract change.
  - The network seam simulates offline inside the app; real radio loss is covered only through the seam's connectivity-event source (unit-tested), not by E2E.

## Phase 3: Lesson-linked practice assignments with auto-grading (core learning loop)

- Outcome (demoable): A teacher writes an MCQ exercise linked to a lesson and assigns it to a class as practice; the student reads the lesson, marks it complete, completes the exercise, and sees a score; the teacher sees that score on the results dashboard, even when the student submitted offline and the outbox synced later.
- Screens: `teacher-exercise-editor` (MCQ questions, optional question images, answer key, linked lesson), `teacher-assignment-editor` (practice type, class, exercise, due date), `teacher-results-dashboard`, `student-assignments`, `student-lesson-and-exercise` (lesson link, mark complete, start exercise), `student-exercise`, `student-exercise-result`
- Backend capabilities:
  - Exercise content (`type: exercise`) with question stems and options plus optional `lessonContentId` pointing to an approved e-book or video; question images stored in MinIO as exercise assets; answer keys in a separate table that is never part of any student-facing model.
  - Tables `assignments`, `submissions`, `progress` (lesson completion: `studentId`, `contentId`, `status`, `updatedAt`).
  - Assignments endpoints: teacher creates, updates, and deletes assignments only for classes they own; student lists assignments only for their own classes; students and parents have no write method.
  - Submissions and progress endpoints: `submissions.submit` accepts only the calling student's own answers for an assignment of their class, keyed by a client-generated submission ID so replays are idempotent; score and grading fields are set only by the server; teacher lists submissions of their own classes; `progress.markComplete` writes only the caller's own progress, idempotently.
  - Auto-grading (the spec's "autoGrade", now server code run inside `submissions.submit`): scores MCQ/objective items against the answer key and stores `score`, `gradedAt`, `gradedBy: auto`, `status: graded`; a grading error stores `status: grading_failed`, is logged, and the teacher can re-run grading with `submissions.regrade`.
  - Outbox in the drift store: progress and submission writes go to the outbox first; a sync worker replays them in order when the network seam reports online, at app start, and on manual retry; a server rejection that retrying cannot fix (for example a denied caller) moves the entry to a named failed state instead of retrying forever.
  - Offline exercises: opening an assignment downloads the exercise and its question images into the content cache.
- Exit criteria:
  1. E2E (spec flow 1): student opens an assignment, opens its linked e-book lesson from `student-lesson-and-exercise`, marks it complete (a `progress` row exists on the server), completes the exercise, submits, and sees the auto-graded score on `student-exercise-result`.
  2. E2E (spec flow 2): teacher creates an exercise and a practice assignment for a class; after the seeded student submits, the teacher sees that student's score and status `statusGraded` (vi: "Đã chấm") on `teacher-results-dashboard`.
  3. E2E: student opens an exercise online, then with the network seam offline completes and submits it; `student-assignments` shows l10n key `submissionPendingSync` (vi: "Bài nộp đang chờ đồng bộ"), driven by the pending outbox entry; the test closes the drift database and re-creates the app root (in-process restart from the on-disk store), the indicator is still shown, then switches the seam online, and the submission syncs, is graded, and the status changes to `statusGraded`.
  4. Server integration test: replaying the same submission ID twice (an outbox retry after a lost response) stores one submission and one grade.
  5. E2E: an exercise never opened online shows `contentNeedsInternet` while offline; an exercise with question images opened online renders its images while offline.
  6. Server integration test: when grading fails (for example a missing answer key), the submission gets `grading_failed`, the failure is logged, the teacher sees `statusGradingFailed` (vi: "Chưa chấm được") with a `retry` action that calls `submissions.regrade`, the student sees `statusSubmittedAwaitingGrade` (vi: "Đã nộp, đang chờ chấm"), and regrade produces a score.
  7. Unit tests: grading covers all-correct, all-wrong, partial, unanswered items, single-select vs multi-select, duplicate submission, and answer-key edits after submission; grading logic coverage is at least 80%; outbox unit tests cover ordering, idempotent replay, and the permanent-failure state.
  8. Server authorization tests (allowed and denied caller per method): student cannot set `score`, `gradedAt`, `gradedBy`, or `status`; student cannot read another student's submission; no student-facing response contains answer-key data (asserted on the serialized responses); student cannot submit to an assignment of a class they are not in; teacher cannot read submissions or run regrade outside their classes.
  9. Server authorization tests (assignments): teacher creating or editing an assignment for another teacher's class is denied; student listing assignments never sees another class's assignment; students and parents calling any assignment write method are denied; authorization code coverage stays at least 80%.
  10. Flutter accessibility guideline tests pass on every phase 3 screen; every status is shown as an l10n word, not color or icon alone.
- Depends on: Phase 2
- Risks:
  - Grading at submit time against an answer key the teacher edited after the student answered offline; the contract must fix which key version grades.
  - Answer-key isolation is now a serialization boundary; one student-facing model that embeds the key leaks answers, so it needs the response-level test in criterion 8.
  - The outbox is app code, not a managed SDK feature; ordering, idempotency, and failure states are where bugs will live.
  - The in-process restart (drift closed and reopened plus root re-create) approximates a process kill; if it proves unrepresentative, the harness needs an adb-driven relaunch.

## Phase 4: AI study tutor through the tutor endpoint (aiProxy)

- Outcome (demoable): A student opens the AI tutor for one of their class subjects, asks a study question in Vietnamese, and watches the answer stream in; an off-topic or out-of-scope request is declined; after the daily limit the tutor says so; offline the tutor shows that it needs internet; every exchange appears in `aiChats`, written by the server.
- Screens: `student-ai-tutor` (subject picker from the student's class subjects, conversation list of past chats, streaming chat, named states: needs internet, daily limit reached, error with retry)
- Backend capabilities:
  - Tutor endpoint streaming method `tutor.ask` (authenticated, student role only) that: builds the system prompt from the requested subject and the class's `gradeLevel` (study help only, no off-topic chat, refuses to solve test questions, age-appropriate tone, replies in Vietnamese); rejects subjects not in the `subjects[]` of the student's classes (topic allowlist); enforces the per-student daily limit with an atomic PostgreSQL counter (server config, default 30 per day, day boundary Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh); reads the OpenRouter model ID from server config and the key from `config/passwords.yaml`; streams the response; logs the exchange to `aiChats`.
  - OpenRouter client behind an interface; the mock is used in all tests and by default in the local stack; a real key in the git-ignored `config/passwords.yaml` switches the local server to real OpenRouter.
  - `tutor.chats` (student: own chats) and `tutor.classChats` (teacher: chats of students in their own classes); no client method writes `aiChats` or the rate-limit counter.
- Exit criteria:
  1. E2E: student picks a subject and sends a question in `student-ai-tutor`; the mocked response renders incrementally (at least two chunks observed before completion); after leaving and reopening the screen, the chat appears in the conversation list and opens with both messages.
  2. Server integration test: the request sent to the mocked OpenRouter contains a system prompt naming the student's subject and class grade level and uses the model ID from server config; changing the config changes the model with no client change.
  3. Server integration test: a request for a subject outside the student's classes' `subjects[]` is rejected with a named error and nothing is sent to OpenRouter.
  4. Server integration test: the 31st message in one Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh day is rejected with a named limit error (UI: `aiDailyLimitReached`, vi: "Bạn đã dùng hết lượt hỏi hôm nay"); the counter resets at local midnight (tested with an injected clock across 23:59 to 00:00 ICT); concurrent requests never exceed the limit; rate-limit logic coverage is at least 80%.
  5. Server integration test: every successful exchange writes the `aiChats` entry with student ID, subject, both messages, and timestamp; a failed or cut-off exchange is logged server-side, and whether it counts against the limit is fixed by the contract and asserted by a test.
  6. E2E: with the network seam offline, `student-ai-tutor` shows `aiTutorNeedsInternet` (vi: "Gia sư AI cần kết nối mạng") and sending is disabled; with the mock forced to time out, the UI shows `aiTutorError` with a `retry` action, and retry succeeds.
  7. Server authorization tests (allowed and denied caller per method): a teacher or parent calling `tutor.ask` is rejected with a named permission error; a student cannot read another student's chats; a teacher can read chats of a student in their class and is denied for a student outside their classes; no endpoint method writes `aiChats` or the counter on a client's behalf except `tutor.ask`.
  8. Static check: the built APK and the Flutter source contain no OpenRouter key or OpenRouter URL; `config/passwords.yaml` is listed in `.gitignore`, and the committed `config/passwords.example.yaml` contains no OpenRouter key.
- Depends on: Phase 1 (classes with `gradeLevel` and `subjects[]`, streaming path proven); scheduled after Phase 3 by order only.
- Risks:
  - Logging after a stream is cut mid-way (partial answers, client disconnect from the WebSocket) needs a contract rule.
  - Model answers in Vietnamese for young students vary by model; the mock cannot test quality (spec open risk).

## Phase 5: Timed test room with online start, auto-submit, and AI lockout

- Outcome (demoable): A teacher creates a short MCQ test; the student starts it online, the AI tutor shows it is paused, the timer runs out, and the test auto-submits and is graded; a second run with the network cut mid-test keeps saving answers, shows pending sync, and auto-submits on reconnect; a submission arriving after the grace window is graded and flagged late.
- Screens: `teacher-assignment-editor` (extended with test type, time limit, question set), `student-test-lobby` (rules, time limit, start action, online-required state), `student-test-room` (questions, local countdown, submit), `student-test-submitted` (submitted, pending sync, graded, or late status), plus the paused state in `student-ai-tutor`
- Backend capabilities:
  - Assignment field `timeLimitSec` for tests; submission lifecycle `in_progress|submitted|graded|grading_failed` with server `startedAt` and server `submittedAt`.
  - `tests.start` endpoint method: requires connectivity by design (it is never queued in the outbox), checks enrollment and that no other test is in progress, creates the `in_progress` submission with server `startedAt`; `submissions.submit` rejects a test submission that has no started record.
  - Local timer derived from `startedAt` (not a running counter), with auto-submit on expiry, surviving backgrounding and in-process restart; answers saved to the drift store on every change; the final submit goes through the outbox, so it is delivered on reconnect.
  - Late flag: `submittedAt` is the server's receipt time (an outbox-delivered submit is timed when it reaches the server); grading marks `late: true` when `submittedAt` is after `startedAt + timeLimitSec + grace` (grace is server config); late submissions are accepted, never rejected.
  - Tutor lockout: `tutor.ask` rejects every request while the student has an `in_progress` test submission, so no `aiChats` entry can be written during a test.
- Exit criteria:
  1. E2E (spec flow 3): student starts a seeded short test, answers some items, and lets the timer expire; the test auto-submits with no user action, `student-test-submitted` shows the graded score, and the teacher dashboard shows the result.
  2. E2E: with the network seam offline, `student-test-lobby` shows `testNeedsInternetToStart` (vi: "Cần kết nối mạng để bắt đầu bài kiểm tra") and the start action is disabled.
  3. E2E: while a test is in progress, `student-ai-tutor` shows `aiTutorPausedDuringTest` (vi: "Gia sư AI tạm dừng trong lúc làm bài kiểm tra"); server integration test: a direct `tutor.ask` call for that student is rejected and no `aiChats` row is written; after submission the tutor works again.
  4. E2E: the network seam goes offline mid-test; answers keep saving locally; on expiry the screen shows `submissionPendingSync`; after switching online the outbox delivers the submission automatically, it is graded, and the status changes to `statusGraded`.
  5. E2E: during a test the app performs the in-process restart (drift closed and reopened plus root re-create); the student returns to `student-test-room` with saved answers and remaining time computed from `startedAt`; when the injected clock is already past expiry, the test auto-submits on re-create.
  6. Server integration test: a submission received after `startedAt + timeLimitSec + grace` is graded and carries `late: true`, and the teacher dashboard shows `statusLate` (vi: "Nộp muộn"); one inside the window carries `late: false`.
  7. Server authorization and integration tests: a student cannot submit a test without `tests.start`, cannot set `startedAt`, `submittedAt`, or `timeLimitSec` through any method, cannot reopen a submitted test, and cannot hold two in-progress tests; `tests.start` is denied for a class the student is not in.
  8. Unit tests: timer logic (remaining time, expiry, clock-skew bounds) and the lockout check; combined grading, rate-limit, lockout, and authorization coverage is at least 80%; Flutter accessibility guideline tests pass on every phase 5 screen, and the countdown is announced to screen readers at fixed intervals, not every second.
- Depends on: Phase 3 (submissions, auto-grading, outbox), Phase 4 (tutor endpoint)
- Risks:
  - Timed tests with real timers are slow and flaky; the contract must define an injectable clock for app and server.
  - The local timer can be gamed on-device; the server-side late flag is the only backstop, by the user's decision.

## Phase 6: Parent summary, teacher AI chat review, and release gate

- Outcome (demoable): A parent signs in and reads the linked child's assignment and test results and full AI tutor transcripts, with no way to change anything; a teacher reviews the AI chat log of a student in their class; the full suite (three spec E2E flows, server integration and authorization tests) passes in one run with coverage gates met.
- Screens: `parent-summary` (replaces the phase 1 placeholder), `parent-ai-chat-log`, `teacher-ai-chat-review`
- Backend capabilities:
  - Parent endpoint `parent.summary` and `parent.chats`: read-only, limited to the caller's `linkedStudentId`; the summary response carries each submission's assignment title, type, score, and status (joined on the server), so the parent needs no access to assignment or content endpoints; parents have no write method anywhere.
  - Teacher chat read (`tutor.classChats`) is already in place from phase 4.
  - Release hardening: one e2e run executes all three spec E2E flows plus every earlier phase's E2E tests; the coverage report for grading, rate-limit, lockout, and authorization code is checked against the 80% threshold.
- Exit criteria:
  1. E2E: seeded parent sees the child's practice and test results on `parent-summary`, each with title, score, and an l10n status word (submitted, pending, graded, late); opening `parent-ai-chat-log` shows the child's chats by subject and date, and each opens as a full read-only transcript.
  2. E2E: `parent-summary` and `parent-ai-chat-log` offer no create, edit, or delete action; server authorization tests confirm every write method in the server denies a parent caller.
  3. Server authorization tests: a parent cannot read an unlinked student's results or chats, and is denied on assignment, content, progress, and class endpoints.
  4. E2E: teacher opens `teacher-ai-chat-review` for a student in their class and sees that student's logged chats as read-only transcripts.
  5. Full suite: the e2e command runs spec flows 1, 2, and 3 green in one run on a freshly seeded stack, three consecutive times with no flake.
  6. Coverage: grading, rate-limit, lockout, and authorization code each report at least 80%; the authorization matrix check passes for every endpoint method; the report is saved under `docs/build/phase-6/evidence/`.
  7. Flutter accessibility guideline tests pass on every screen in the app, and the literal-string l10n test passes for all of `edubox_flutter/lib/`.
- Depends on: Phase 3, Phase 4, Phase 5
- Risks:
  - The parent feature set is a stub by design; requests for notifications, detailed reports, or lesson progress are out of scope and need their own brainstorming pass.

## Rulings and decisions

- 2026-10-29 User decision: toolchain -> the user installs Flutter, JDK, Android SDK, and the Firebase CLI; the pipeline does not install them. (Superseded by the toolchain decision for the Serverpod backend below.)
- 2026-10-29 User decision: backend environment -> emulator-only project `demo-edubox`, no real cloud project, no billing; OpenRouter mocked, with an optional real key in git-ignored `functions/.secret.local`. (Superseded by the backend decision below.)
- 2026-10-29 User decision: git -> commit on `phase-N` branches; merge to `master` after a passed gate.
- 2026-10-29 User decision: UI language -> Vietnamese, built on Flutter l10n (ARB) so more languages can be added later.
- 2026-10-29 User decision: provisioning -> seed/admin script creates email/password accounts, sets the role claim, and links each student to one parent; no sign-up screen. (With the Serverpod backend the role is a column in the server's `users` table, not a claim.)
- 2026-10-29 User decision: content approval and scope -> `content` has `status: draft|approved` and `classIds[]`; the owning teacher approves explicitly.
- 2026-10-29 User decision: AI scope data -> `classes` has `gradeLevel` and `subjects[]`, seeded from phase 1; these drive the topic allowlist and system prompt.
- 2026-10-29 User decision: AI chat logs -> `aiChats` is written only by `aiProxy`; teachers read chats of their own classes; parents read full transcripts of their linked child. (With the Serverpod backend, `aiProxy` is the tutor endpoint `tutor.ask`.)
- 2026-10-29 User decision: AI limit -> default 30 messages per day per student, day boundary Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh, set as a function param. (With the Serverpod backend it is a server config value.)
- 2026-10-29 User decision: tests -> starting a test requires connectivity (server `startedAt`); losing connectivity mid-test is fine; late submissions are accepted and flagged late (after `startedAt` + time limit + grace).
- 2026-10-29 User decision: roadmap (K2) -> approved as written, 6 phases.
- 2026-10-29 User decision: contentIngest scope -> validation plus metadata normalization only, no transcoding.
- 2026-10-29 User decision: parent view -> results and full AI transcripts only, no lesson-completion progress.
- 2026-10-29 User decision: design direction (K3) -> approved docs/design/app-direction.md: achromatic-ledger, accent ink-blue #1F4C8F, Bitter / Be Vietnam Pro / IBM Plex Mono bundled offline.
- 2026-10-29 User decision: phase 1 shape briefs (P1) -> confirmed: only built destinations in nav; rows not tappable in phase 1; student-home greeting + newest 4 + Mở thư viện; sign-out confirm for students only; library grouped by subject incl. exercises; teacher-home class ledger; parent-home name only; account-not-set-up with Kiểm tra lại + Đăng xuất. Briefs in docs/design/shapes/.
- 2026-10-29 User decision: backend -> a self-written Dart server on Serverpod with PostgreSQL and S3-compatible object storage (MinIO locally), all run locally through Docker Compose; the app keeps an offline local store (SQLite via drift) plus an outbox for unsynced writes; supersedes the emulator-only Firebase decision.
- 2026-10-29 User decision: toolchain (Serverpod backend) -> the user installs Flutter, JDK 21, Android SDK with the `edubox_tablet` AVD, Docker (29 installed), and `serverpod_cli`; Firebase CLI and Node are no longer needed; supersedes the earlier toolchain decision.
- 2026-10-29 User decision: implementation executor -> every BE and FE implementation task (P4 build, P7 implementer fixes) runs in the `opencode` CLI on `opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash`; Claude agents do not implement; plans must therefore carry complete code and exact commands per task.
- 2026-10-29 User decision: delivery -> one branch per phase; when a phase passes its gate, push it, open a PR to `main`, and merge after CI is green; the repo has a GitHub Actions CI workflow (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`); `.gitignore` ignores only `.github/hooks/` and keeps `docs/` tracked.
- 2026-10-29 Ruling: PRODUCT.md and the DESIGN.md seed were already approved, so K3 skipped the impeccable interviews.
- 2026-10-29 Ruling: riskiest integrations first - phase 1 proves server-stored roles with server-side authorization, the AVD talking to the compose stack, the drift local store, l10n, a Serverpod streaming method, and MinIO storage end to end before feature work - cost if wrong: late discovery that E2E, streaming, or object storage is unreliable invalidates later exit criteria. (Rewritten 2026-10-29 for the Serverpod backend.)
- 2026-10-29 Ruling: phase cuts, order, outcomes, and screens are unchanged by the backend switch, with one forced move: the drift local store and the network seam move from phase 2 into phase 1, because the confirmed phase 1 shape briefs require offline-with-cache states that Firestore's cache used to provide for free; phase 1 also gains the MinIO storage spike - cost if wrong: phase 1 grows by the local store, which phase 2 would otherwise build.
- 2026-10-29 Ruling: `contentIngest` scope is validation (type, size, readability) plus metadata normalization (MIME, size, page count or duration); it does no transcoding or format conversion, which narrows the spec's "validates/transforms" for the prototype - confirmed by the user. With the Serverpod backend it runs as server code inside `content.completeUpload`.
- 2026-10-29 Ruling: E2E harness - offline is simulated through the app's `NetworkController` seam, which makes every server call fail fast as offline; app restart is simulated in-process by closing the drift database and re-creating the app root, which reopens the store from disk; an unreachable backend is simulated by a test file that points `EDUBOX_SERVER_URL` at a closed port; nothing stops a compose service during a run - cost if wrong: an adb-driven relaunch and airplane-mode harness would be needed. (Rewritten 2026-10-29 for the Serverpod backend.)
- 2026-10-29 Ruling: authorization gate - every EduBox endpoint method has at least one allowed-caller and one denied-caller integration test, including an unauthenticated denial; auth-module methods are listed separately, each either on the explicit unauthenticated exception list (sign-in, plus the module's session refresh method if the chosen session mode has one) with a test, or with a test proving it denies (registration, account requests, password reset); a check fails when a generated endpoint method appears in neither list; authorization code has at least 80% line coverage per `tool/coverage_gate.dart`; this replaces the Firestore rule-coverage report and the Storage rules matrix - cost if wrong: none; it is stricter than a coverage number alone. (Rewritten 2026-10-29 for the Serverpod backend; scoped to EduBox endpoints plus the module exception list after roadmap r2.)
- 2026-10-29 Ruling: offline writes - progress and submission writes go to an outbox table in the drift store and are replayed in order by a sync worker (on reconnect, at app start, and on manual retry); every replayed write carries a client-generated ID and the server handles it idempotently; the "pending sync" indicator is driven by pending outbox entries; a write the server rejects permanently moves to a named failed state; `tests.start` and `tutor.ask` are never queued - why: the spec puts sync in app code now, and each submission has exactly one writer - cost if wrong: phase 3 and 5 contracts change. (Rewritten 2026-10-29; replaces the Firestore offline-persistence assumption.)
- 2026-10-29 Ruling: server work that Firebase ran as triggers or callables becomes Serverpod endpoint methods: auto-grading runs inside `submissions.submit` (re-runnable through `submissions.regrade`), content ingest inside `content.completeUpload`, test start is `tests.start`, the AI proxy is the streaming `tutor.ask`, and the phase 1 streaming proof is `diagnostics.pingStream` - why: there are no database or storage triggers, and running the work in the request makes failures visible to the caller - cost if wrong: a slow ingest or grade may need a Serverpod future call instead. (Rewritten 2026-10-29; replaces the `autoGrade` trigger and `startTest` callable assumption.)
- 2026-10-29 Ruling: files are served through short-lived signed URLs that `content.fileUrl` issues only after an authorization check; the MinIO bucket is private - why: object storage has no per-user rules, so the server is the only gate - cost if wrong: video playback may need the server to proxy byte ranges instead.
- 2026-10-29 Ruling: server configuration (OpenRouter model ID, daily AI limit, day-boundary timezone, late grace, MinIO public endpoint) lives in the server's run-mode config; secrets live in the git-ignored `config/passwords.yaml`, which `tool/bootstrap.sh` creates from the committed `config/passwords.example.yaml`; the example holds only clearly labelled dev-only values for the local stack (database, MinIO, Serverpod auth secrets) and no production section; the real OpenRouter key is never committed and is the only secret a developer adds by hand - why: a clean checkout must run with no hand-made file, and the spec keeps the key server-side - cost if wrong: none. (Rewritten 2026-10-29 after roadmap r2.)
- 2026-10-29 Ruling: compose lifecycle - `up --wait` starts only long-running services (`postgres`, `postgres_test`, `minio`, and in profile `e2e` the `server`, whose healthcheck passes only after migrations are applied); the one-shot `minio-init` (creates buckets) and `seed` (truncates data tables and the auth tables, empties the e2e bucket, re-seeds; never drops the schema) live in profile `tools` and run only through `docker compose run --rm`, after the server is healthy; Redis is disabled - why: `--wait` does not handle exiting services, and a schema drop under a running server breaks it - cost if wrong: none.
- 2026-10-29 ASSUMPTION: the role is loaded server-side from the `users` table for each request, and Serverpod auth scopes are not used for roles, so there is one source of truth; the app routes by the role it gets from `profile.me` and caches it in the drift store for offline display only - why: the spec keeps the role only in the server's `users` table - cost if wrong: none. (Rewritten 2026-10-29; replaces the custom-claim assumption.)
- 2026-10-29 ASSUMPTION: the parent's `users` row carries `linkedStudentId` and `linkedStudentName` (now in the spec's data model), so `parent-home` needs no access to the child's profile, and parent endpoints are limited to the linked child's results and chats - why: matches the spec's parent scope exactly - cost if wrong: small schema change.
- 2026-10-29 ASSUMPTION: exercise questions live on the exercise content (stems and options only), answer keys live in a separate table that no student-facing model includes, and question images are MinIO exercise assets - why: the spec has no question model and students must never read answers - cost if wrong: phase 3 data model rework.
- 2026-10-29 ASSUMPTION: a "lesson" is an e-book or video content item; an exercise links to its lesson through an optional `lessonContentId`; completing a lesson writes a `progress` row (`studentId`, `contentId`, `status`, `updatedAt`) - why: spec flow 1 needs a lesson-to-exercise link and a completion record the data model lacks - cost if wrong: flow 1 and the phase 3 screens change.
- 2026-10-29 ASSUMPTION: submissions get `status` (`in_progress|submitted|graded|grading_failed`), `startedAt`, `submittedAt`, and `late`; assignments get `timeLimitSec` for tests; the late grace is server config (default 60 seconds) - why: the lockout, timed tests, and late flag need fields the data model lacks - cost if wrong: phase 3 and 5 contracts change.
- 2026-10-29 ASSUMPTION: the system prompt keeps a general "do not solve test questions" instruction, but the spec's per-question "flagged test-mode questions" mechanism is dropped; the full tutor lockout during an active test covers it - why: the spec defines no flagging mechanism - cost if wrong: phase 4 adds a teacher-flagged question list.
- 2026-10-29 ASSUMPTION: a teacher web console, the dictionary (in PRODUCT.md, absent from the spec), kiosk mode, short-answer grading, and production hosting are out of scope for this roadmap - why: the spec marks them non-goals or does not specify them - cost if wrong: an extra phase.
- 2026-10-29 ASSUMPTION: every phase's exit includes Flutter accessibility guideline tests on its new screens, and every status is shown as an l10n word - why: PRODUCT.md requires WCAG 2.1 AA and DESIGN.md's Named State Rule - cost if wrong: none.
- 2026-10-29 ASSUMPTION: Vietnamese strings quoted in exit criteria are proposed copy; the l10n key is the contract, and the final text lives in `app_vi.arb` - why: copy can be refined without changing tests, because tests look strings up by key - cost if wrong: none.
- 2026-10-29 Ruling: Serverpod is pinned to 4.0.4 (CLI and every `serverpod*` package, including `serverpod_auth_idp_server`, `serverpod_auth_idp_flutter`, `serverpod_cloud_storage_s3`, and `serverpod_test`), the latest stable release on pub.dev, published 2026-10-06; sign-in uses the `serverpod_auth_idp` email identity provider, not the legacy `serverpod_auth` module - why: the user installs the CLI before the contract exists, and the version decides the auth, storage, and test-tool APIs - cost if wrong: contract churn in phase 1 only. (Replaces the earlier ASSUMPTION that the contract would pin the version.)
- 2026-10-30 Ruling: e2e control route - an on-device integration test cannot run `docker compose run seed`, so the server exposes a token-guarded `e2e.run` that performs reset/seed, the reconnect deltas, and set/clear role; it is enabled only in the compose e2e (`development`) and `test` run modes, and only there when `edubox.e2eControl`/`EDUBOX_E2E_CONTROL` is true; `production`, `staging` and every other run mode reject it even with the env override and the correct token - why: exit criteria 7 and the account-not-set-up check-again need server state to change mid-run, while a production server must never expose the route - cost if wrong: an adb-driven host-side driver would replace it. (Added 2026-10-30; run-mode gate added 2026-10-30 after review r2.)
- 2026-10-30 Ruling: the unauthenticated exception list includes, besides sign-in and JWT refresh, `serverpod_auth_core.status.isSignedIn`/`signOutDevice`/`signOutAllDevices` (session-manager helpers that return false or no-op without a session) and the three `serverpod_cloud_storage` raw routes (public database-backed storage and keyed temporary/upload routes that EduBox never issues keys for); exit criterion 12's no-sign-up assertions still apply to every registration, account-request and password-reset method - why: these are framework/module routes with tested harmless behaviour, not EduBox data access - cost if wrong: a future Serverpod version changes what these routes do. (Recorded 2026-10-30; the matrix already lists and tests them.)
- 2026-10-30 Ruling: the storage implementation uses `serverpod_cloud_storage_s3_compat` 4.0.4 instead of `serverpod_cloud_storage_s3` - why: criterion 10 needs a configurable endpoint, path-style addressing for MinIO, and signing for a public host different from the internal one; the s3 package cannot do that - cost if wrong: the storage spike falls back to a small custom S3 client. (Replaces the package named in the phase 1 backend capability and risk.)
- 2026-10-30 Ruling: offline session restore - `restoreSession` tries the auth session manager, and when that needs a server round trip while the seam is offline it falls back to the cached session in the drift store (render-only, never authorization); the E2E restart flow keeps criterion 5 - why: the module may refresh online before restoring, and phase 1 must survive a cold offline start - cost if wrong: the real binding needs its own persisted token handling in phase 2.
